one_liner: Post-train a 100M base model with SFT, DPO, and narrow GRPO/RLVR into a stopping, preference-tuned, arithmetic-capable assistant.

key_terms.definition: Cross-entropy training on rendered chat conversations, with loss masked to assistant tokens only, that teaches a base model to take turns and stop.
The fixed rendering of role turns (system/user/assistant) into token sequences using reserved special tokens like <|user|>, <|assistant|>, and <|end|>.
Setting the label to an ignore index (-100) on every non-assistant token so cross-entropy gradients flow only through assistant content and its closing <|end|>.
A logistic loss over preference pairs (chosen, rejected) that raises the policy's log-probability of the winner relative to a frozen reference, with no reward model or rollouts.
The frozen SFT model used as the baseline in DPO's and GRPO's log-ratio/KL terms; log-probs under it can be precomputed and cached since it never changes.
Reinforcement learning where a program (e.g., an exact-match checker) grades model samples for correctness, replacing a learned, hackable reward model.
A critic-free RL algorithm that samples a group of G completions per prompt and uses the group's own reward mean/std as the advantage baseline, optimized with a PPO-style clipped surrogate.
The standardized reward within a sampled group, Â_i = (R_i - mean(R))/(std(R)+ε), broadcast to every token of that response as its training signal.
The failure mode where RL yields zero gradient because every sampled response in a group gets the same reward (all-correct or all-wrong), so advantages vanish.
Erasure of pretrained knowledge/fluency caused by using too large a learning rate during post-training, which is why SFT/DPO/GRPO use small LRs on a converged model.

A policy exploiting a proxy reward (e.g., emitting the answer-format marker without correct reasoning) to score well without achieving the intended goal, mitigated by KL leashes and small format penalties.
An unbiased, low-variance, always-non-negative estimator of KL divergence, exp(logr) - logr - 1, used as the KL penalty term in the GRPO loss.

prerequisites: causal language model pretraining and cross-entropy loss
the attention mechanism and document-aware/packed attention masking
policy gradients and PPO's clipped surrogate objective
KL divergence and Bradley-Terry preference modeling
